children: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL), now led by CEO John Ternus, is juggling a major product push—new iPhones, AirPods and a limited‑run foldable—while navigating rising Pro iPhone BOMs, legal and regulatory probes over App Store and privacy rules, and efforts to expand Siri and Apple AI amid supply constraints.
Previous Week Recap
John Ternus Named CEO

: Apple (AAPL) named John Ternus CEO; his tasks include boosting Siri, courting developers for Siri integrations, advancing Apple AI amid component shortages, and handling related supply‑chain issues.
Foldable iPhone Event Launch
: Apple (AAPL) unveiled a foldable phone, new iPhone models and updated AirPods at its Sept. 9 Cupertino event — the first product launch under CEO John Ternus.
Limited Foldable iPhone Production

: Apple (AAPL) started limited foldable iPhone production, making a few hundred units daily under tight quality controls; the company aims to build 8–10 million foldables this year amid early ramp-up.
App Store Fee Ruling Hit
: Apple (AAPL): App Store fee ruling and tougher competition cut in‑app purchase revenue, slowing services growth and reducing App Store commission income in the June quarter.
Rising BOM For Pro iPhone
: AAPL faces rising bill-of-materials for the Pro iPhone as memory chip costs jump on AI data-center demand; BOM up about 40% YoY and talks of roughly $200 higher pricing.
£2B Class Action Filed
: Apple (AAPL) faces a £2B class action in London claiming App Tracking Transparency favored Apple’s ads and cut developers’ ad revenue; shares fell about 0.35% in premarket trade.
Face ID Patents Suit
: BASF’s trinamiX sued Apple over seven Face ID patents in U.S. court, targeting multiple iPhone and iPad Pro models, seeking damages and an injunction; AAPL shares fell about 1.1% after filing.
EU Probes Data Rules
: EU regulators in Germany, France, Italy and Poland are probing Apple (AAPL) over data-consent rules and App Store practices, including recent German-mandated tweaks to its data-consent policies.
Services Margin At 75.6%
: AAPL's Services gross margin hit 75.6% in June 2026; company-wide gross margin rose from 40.5% in 2011 to 50.1% by that quarter, reflecting shift toward higher-margin services.
Ex-Employee Schematic Disclosure
: Apple says forensic review of ex-employee Chang Liu’s MacBook shows he downloaded a confidential Apple circuit schematic, used it at OpenAI, and kept unauthorized access after leaving.
